arxiv-2112-04387.title: Truth-tracking via Approval Voting: Size Matters
arxiv-2112-04387.creator: Tahar Allouche, Jérôme Lang, Florian Yger
arxiv-2112-04387.description: Abstract Epistemic social choice aims at unveiling a hidden ground truth given votes, which are interpreted as noisy signals about it. We consider here a simple setting where votes consist of approval ballots: each voter approves a set of alternatives which they believe can possibly be the ground truth.

arxiv-2202-00383.title: Explainable AI through the Learning of Arguments
arxiv-2202-00383.creator: Jonas Bei, David Pomerenke, Lukas Schreiner, Sepideh Sharbaf, Pieter Collins, Nico Roos 1
arxiv-2202-00383.description: Abstract Learning arguments is highly relevant to the field of explainable artificial intelligence. It is a family of symbolic machine learning techniques that is particularly human-interpretable. These techniques learn a set of arguments as an intermediate representation. Arguments are small rules with exceptions that can be chained to larger arguments for making predictions or decisions.

arxiv-2206-00682.title: SDSS IV MaNGA: Characteristics of Edge-on Galaxies with a Counter-rotating Gaseous Disk 2022 SDSS IV MaNGA: Characteristics of Edge-on Galaxies with a Counter-rotating Gaseous Disk – References
arxiv-2206-00682.creator: Minje Beom, Dmitry Bizyaev, René A. M. Walterbos, Yanmei Chen
arxiv-2206-00682.description: Abstract Counter-rotating components in galaxies are one of the most direct forms of evidence for past gas accretion or merging. We discovered ten edge-on disk gaseous counter-rotators in a sample of 523 edge-on galaxies identified in the final MaNGA (Mapping Nearby Galaxies at APO) IFU sample. The counter-rotators tend to located in small groups.

arxiv-2212-02005.title: On the Paley graph of a quadratic character Thanks: Jan Minac is partially supported by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) grant R0370A01. Jan Minac also gratefully acknowledges Faculty of Sciences Distinguished Research Professorship award for 2020/21. Jan Minac
arxiv-2212-02005.creator: Ján Mináč, Lyle Muller, Tung T. Nguyen, Nguy Ê ~ \tilde{\text{\^{E}}} n Duy Tân
arxiv-2212-02005.description: Abstract . Paley graphs form a nice link between the distribution of quadratic residues and graph theory. These graphs possess remarkable properties which make them useful in several branches of mathematics. Classically, for each prime number p p we can construct the corresponding Paley graph using quadratic and non-quadratic residues modulo p p .

arxiv-2303-06190.title: Pion stars embedded in neutrino clouds
arxiv-2303-06190.creator: O. S. Stashko, O. V. Savchuk, L. M. Satarov, I. N. Mishustin, M. I. Gorenstein, V. I. Zhdanov
arxiv-2303-06190.description: Abstract We study self-gravitating multi-pion systems (pion stars) in a state of the Bose condensate. To ensure stability of such stars, it is assumed that they are immersed in the lepton background. Two different phenomenological equations of state (EoS) for the pion matter are used, some of them having the first order phase transition.

arxiv-2310-01120.title: Evaluating Three Levels of Quantum Metrics on Quantum-Inspire Hardware
arxiv-2310-01120.creator: Ward van der Schoot, Robert Wezeman, Pieter Thijs Eendebak, Niels M. P. Neumann, Frank Phillipson
arxiv-2310-01120.description: Abstract With the rise of quantum computing, many quantum devices have been developed and many more devices are being developed as we speak. This begs the question of which device excels at which tasks and how to compare these different quantum devices with one another. The answer is given by quantum metrics , of which many exist today already.

arxiv-2407-16761.title: Continued developments in X-ray speed reading: fast, low noise readout for next-generation wide-field imagers
arxiv-2407-16761.creator: Sven Herrmann, Peter Orel, Tanmoy Chattopadhyay, Glenn Morris, Gregory Prigozhin, Haley R. Stueber, Steven W. Allen, Marshall W. Bautz, Kevan Donlon, Beverly LaMarr, Chris Leitz, Eric Miller, Abigail Pan, Artem Poliszczuk, Daniel R. Wilkins
arxiv-2407-16761.description: Abstract Future strategic X-ray astronomy missions will require unprecedentedly sensitive wide-field imagers providing high frame rates, low readout noise and excellent soft energy response. To meet these needs, our team is employing a multi-pronged approach to advance several key areas of technology.

arxiv-2408-03016.title: Can a naked singularity be formed during the gravitational collapse of a Janis-Newman-Winicour solution?
arxiv-2408-03016.creator: Xiao Yan Chew a , Il Gyeong Choi b , Hyuk Jung Kim and Dong-han Yeom b,c,d
arxiv-2408-03016.description: Abstract The Janis-Newman-Winicour (JNW) spacetime possesses a naked singularity, although it represents an exact particle-like solution to the Einstein-Klein-Gordon theory with a massless scalar field. Here, we investigate the possible formation of a naked singularity in the JNW spacetime, using the thin-shell approximation to describe the gravitational collapse.

arxiv-2502-05581.title: Dynamical mechanism of vacuum energy compensation
arxiv-2502-05581.creator: E.V. Arbuzova, A.D. Dolgov
arxiv-2502-05581.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by E.V. Arbuzova, A.D. Dolgov. The model of vacuum energy compensation due to interaction of a scalar field ϕ \phi with curvature scalar of the form β ​ R ​ ϕ 2 ​ f ​ ( ϕ ) \beta R\phi^{2}f(\phi) is proposed.

arxiv-2509-19086.title: Scheduler-Driven Job Atomization
arxiv-2509-19086.creator: Michal Konopa, Jan Fesl, Ladislav Beránek
arxiv-2509-19086.description: Abstract Modern GPU clusters, particularly those built on NVIDIA’s Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) architecture, often suffer from inefficiencies because jobs are treated as rigid, indivisible blocks that occupy a fixed slice until completion. The reliance on static peak memory estimates exacerbates fragmentation, underutilization, and job rejections.

arxiv-2601-23178.title: Forward and Inverse Mantle Convection with Neural Operators
arxiv-2601-23178.creator: Chenxi Kong 1, Michael Gurnis 1 and Zachary E. Ross 1 1 Seismological Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA 91125, USA
arxiv-2601-23178.description: Abstract keywords Mantle convection, Inverse Theory, Machine Learning, Neural Operators, Dynamic System. {summary} Thermal state reconstruction—reversing convection to recover the thermal structure of the mantle at an earlier geologic time—is an important tool to understand the evolution of mantle convection and its relation to seismic tomographic images and observations at the surface. Thermal state reconstructions are computationally expensive.

arxiv-2602-03430.title: ProAct: A Benchmark and Multimodal Framework for Structure-Aware Proactive Response
arxiv-2602-03430.creator: Xiaomeng Zhu, Fengming Zhu, Weijie Zhou, Ye Tian, Zhenlin Hu, Yufei Huang, Yuchun Guo, Xinyu Wu, Zhengyou Zhang, Fangzhen Lin, Xuantang Xiong
arxiv-2602-03430.description: Abstract While passive agents merely follow instructions, proactive agents align with higher-level objectives, such as assistance and safety by continuously monitoring the environment to determine when and how to act. However, developing proactive agents is hindered by the lack of specialized resources.

arxiv-2602-13286.title: Explanatory Interactive Machine Learning for Bias Mitigation in Visual Gender Classification
arxiv-2602-13286.creator: Nathanya Queby Satriani, Djordje Slijepčević, Markus Schedl, Matthias Zeppelzauer
arxiv-2602-13286.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Nathanya Queby Satriani, Djordje Slijepčević, Markus Schedl, Matthias Zeppelzauer. Explanatory interactive learning (XIL) enables users to guide model training in machine learning (ML) by providing feedback on the model’s explanations, thereby helping it to focus on features that are relevant to the prediction from the user’s perspective. In this study, we explore the capability of this learning paradigm to mitigate bias and spurious correlations in visual classifiers, specifically in scenarios prone to data bias, such as gender classification.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-vicenza.title: Vicenza (Catholic Encyclopedia article)
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-vicenza.creator: Umberto Benigni
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-vicenza.description: Article 'Vicenza' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

europmc-pmc3948040.title: Arsenic exposure perturbs the gut microbiome and its metabolic profile in mice: an integrated metagenomics and metabolomics analysis.
europmc-pmc3948040.creator: Lu K, Abo RP, Schlieper KA, Graffam ME, Levine S, Wishnok JS, Swenberg JA, Tannenbaum SR, Fox JG.
europmc-pmc3948040.description: Background The human intestine is host to an enormously complex, diverse, and vast microbial community-the gut microbiota. The gut microbiome plays a profound role in metabolic processing, energy production, immune and cognitive development, epithelial homeostasis, and so forth.

pmc-10654230.title: Contextual attributes associated with public participation in environmental impact assessments in Thailand: Perspectives obtained from authorities and academics
pmc-10654230.creator: Kanang Kantamaturapoj, Chaunjit Chanchitpricha, Parinee Hongsuwan, Pannipa Suebsing, Suwicha Thaweesuk, Suwit Wibulpolprasert
pmc-10654230.description: Context can enhance or hinder public participation (PP) in environmental impact assessments (EIAs). This study aimed to investigate and discuss how PP-related contextual attributes influence the quality of PP in Thai EIA processes. The study adopted the qualitative approach and interviewed 20 key informants with insightful PP-associated experience in Thai EIAs.

pmc-10719591.title: An Innovative Chemical Adherence Test Demonstrates Very High Rates of Nonadherence to Oral Cardio-Metabolic Medications
pmc-10719591.creator: Hanad Osman, Dan Lane, Dennis Bernieh, Samuel Seidu, Prashanth Patel, Kamlesh Khunti, Nigel J Brunskill, Gang Xu, Pankaj Gupta
pmc-10719591.description: tes due to CKD.1,2 Compared to patients without CKD, CKD stages G3a to G4 (estimated glomerular filtration rate 15–60 ml/min per 1.73 m2) is associated with a 2 to 3 fold increase in risk of cardiovascular disease mortality.3 It is estimated that about 17% to 74% of patients with CKD are nonadherent to their medications.

pmc-11332917.title: Tele-medicine controlled hospital at home is associated with better outcomes than hospital stay
pmc-11332917.creator: Noa Zychlinski, Ronen Fluss, Yair Goldberg, Daniel Zubli, Galia Barkai, Eyal Zimlichman, Gad Segal, Filomena Pietrantonio, Filomena Pietrantonio, Filomena Pietrantonio
pmc-11332917.description: BackgroundHospital-at-home (HAH) is increasingly becoming an alternative for in-hospital stay in selected clinical scenarios. Nevertheless, there is still a question whether HAH could be a viable option for acutely ill patients, otherwise hospitalized in departments of general-internal medicine.MethodsThis was a retrospective matched study, conducted at a telemedicine controlled HAH department, being part of a tertiary medical center.

pmc-11453078.title: Association of socioeconomic status and life’s essential 8 with cardiovascular diseases and all-cause mortality in north China: Kailuan study
pmc-11453078.creator: Jiwen Zhong, Qing Cai, Wei Zheng, Shuohua Chen, Shouling Wu, Shaohong Dong
pmc-11453078.description: BackgroundWe aimed to explore the association of socioeconomic status (SES) and life’s essential 8 (LE8) with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and all-cause mortality in north China.MethodsA total of 91,365 adults from the Kailuan study were included in this study. Comprehensive individual SES, mainly including monthly household income, education, Occupation position, and community environment, was confirmed by latent class analysis.

pmc-11462571.title: Neuroimaging and the Investigation of Drug-Drug Interactions Involving Psychedelics
pmc-11462571.creator: Matthew B Wall, Rebecca Harding, Natalie Ertl, Tommaso Barba, Rayyan Zafar, Mark Sweeney, David J Nutt, Eugenii A Rabiner, David Erritzoe
pmc-11462571.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Psychedelic therapies are an emerging class of treatments in psychiatry with great potential, however relatively little is known about their interactions with other commonly used psychiatric medications. As psychedelic therapies become more widespread and move closer to the clinic, they likely will need to be integrated into existing treatment models which may include one or more traditional pharmacological therapies, meaning an awareness of potential drug-drug interactions will become vital.

pmc-11472905.title: Sex Differences in Skeletal Muscle Pathology in Patients With Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction
pmc-11472905.creator: Nathanael Wood, Annabel Critchlow, Chew W. Cheng, Sam Straw, Paul W. Hendrickse, Marcelo G. Pereira, Stephen B. Wheatcroft, Stuart Egginton, Klaus K. Witte, Lee D. Roberts, T. Scott Bowen
pmc-11472905.description: BACKGROUND:Women with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) have greater symptoms and a lower quality of life compared with men; however, the role of noncardiac mechanisms remains poorly resolved. We hypothesized that differences in skeletal muscle pathology between men and women with HFrEF may explain clinical heterogeneity.

pmc-11476080.title: Predicting stroke occurrences: a stacked machine learning approach with feature selection and data preprocessing
pmc-11476080.creator: Pritam Chakraborty, Anjan Bandyopadhyay, Preeti Padma Sahu, Aniket Burman, Saurav Mallik, Najah Alsubaie, Mohamed Abbas, Mohammed S. Alqahtani, Ben Othman Soufiene
pmc-11476080.description: Stroke prediction remains a critical area of research in healthcare, aiming to enhance early intervention and patient care strategies. This study investigates the efficacy of machine learning techniques, particularly principal component analysis (PCA) and a stacking ensemble method, for predicting stroke occurrences based on demographic, clinical, and lifestyle factors.

pmc-11615250.title: Modeling carbon intensity of electric vehicles in the well-to-wheels phase under different traffic flow conditions
pmc-11615250.creator: Yaping Dong, Xin Guo, Meng Wang, Jinliang Xu
pmc-11615250.description: SummaryWith the proliferation of electric vehicles (EVs), accurately assessing their well-to-wheels carbon intensity is crucial. In this study, a quadratic model was developed, integrating a top-down carbon accounting approach with field test data, to quantify the carbon intensity of electric vehicles under various traffic flow conditions.

pmc-11660328.title: Blocking IL1RAP on cancer-associated fibroblasts in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma suppresses IL-1-induced neutrophil recruitment
pmc-11660328.creator: Nils Hansen, Pablo Peña-Martínez, Petter Skoog, Katrin Reinbach, Finja C Hansen, Susanne Larsson Faria, Caitríona Grönberg, Kawther Abdilleh, Susanne Magnusson, Karin von Wachenfeldt, Camilla Rydberg Millrud, David Liberg, Marcus Järås
pmc-11660328.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) represents a major clinical challenge due to its tumor microenvironment, which exhibits immune-suppressive properties that facilitate cancer progression, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Interleukin 1 (IL-1) signaling has been implicated as a driver in this process. Mechanistically, both IL-1α and IL-1β bind to the IL-1 receptor type 1, forming a complex with IL-1-receptor accessory protein (IL1RAP), which triggers downstream signaling pathways.

pmc-11677841.title: The Effect of Cropping Systems on the Dispersal of Mycotoxigenic Fungi by Insects in Pre-Harvest Maize in Kenya
pmc-11677841.creator: Ginson M Riungu, James Muthomi, Maina Wagacha, Wolfgang Buechs, Esther S Philip, Torsten Meiners, George N Mbata
pmc-11677841.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryOngoing climate change has led to increased insect damage to maize and the mycotoxigenic fungal infestation and subsequent mycotoxin contamination of maize meant for food and feed. A field study was conducted in two regions in Kenya to see how different maize–legume cropping systems affect the arthropod taxa that were most prevalent on maize at the flowering and grain-filling stages, the arthropods that were most damaging, those that could potentially disperse mycotoxigenic fungi on pre-harvest maize, and the aflatoxin contamination of

pmc-12397999.title: Physical Performance Tests in 8008 Competitive Youth Tennis Players—A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of Normative Values
pmc-12397999.creator: Sebastian Axman, Martin B Stausholm, Nicola Reiner Volk, Alexander Ferrauti, S P Magnusson, Christian Couppé
pmc-12397999.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Normative values for physical performance tests (PTESTs) offer insights into athletes' profiles on strengths and weaknesses to enhance performance and mitigate injury risks. However, such data for youth tennis players have not previously been compiled in a systematic review. We conducted a systematic review of 17 popular PTESTs covering speed, agility, strength, and power in healthy, competitive youth tennis players under the age of 8–18 years.

pmc-12416809.title: Unseen scars: a case report on clitoral epidermal inclusion cyst and its influence on female body perception
pmc-12416809.creator: Qudus Olajide Lawal, Ade Isenalumhe, Governor B O Okome, Mojeed Momoh, Joseph Ikheloa, Charles Igene, Sharon Emordi, Julius Arebun
pmc-12416809.description: Clitoral cyst is an epidermal inclusion cyst that results from invagination of the epidermis into the dermis or subcutaneous tissue. It commonly occurs following trauma from female genital mutilation (FGM), with presentation typically in childhood or the peripubertal period. Later, presentations often arise due to the asymptomatic nature of the condition and the associated stigma.

pmc-12617556.title: Development and validation of a computational tool to predict treatment outcomes in cells from high‐grade serous ovarian cancer patients
pmc-12617556.creator: Marilisa Cortesi, Dongli Liu, Elyse Powell, Ellen Barlow, Kristina Warton, Emanuele Giordano, Caroline E Ford
pmc-12617556.description: Treatment of High‐grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is often ineffective due to frequent late‐stage diagnosis and development of resistance to therapy. Timely selection of the most effective (combination of) drug(s) for each patient would improve outcomes, however the tools currently available to clinicians are poorly suited to the task.

pmc-12699169.title: Extracellular Vesicles Released From Prostate Cancer Cells Confer Pro‐Tumor Properties to Adipocytes by Stimulating Lipolysis
pmc-12699169.creator: Gaia Giannitti, Kinga Kamińska, Sara Marchesi, Riccardo Garavaglia, Ivan Preosto, Małgorzata Grzesiak, Fabrizio Fontana
pmc-12699169.description: There is consistent evidence of an association between obesity and the risk of prostate cancer (PCa). A crosstalk between PCa and adipocytes has been highlighted; however, the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in this communication still needs to be elucidated.

pmc-13239939.title: Case Report: Recurrent Guillain–Barré Syndrome in a 56‐Year‐Old Male
pmc-13239939.creator: Farah Sadiq, Shayan Nawaz, Moeez Ahmad Saeed, Fahad Bilal, Hafiza Manahil Majeed, Wasfa Shafiq, Kashaf Imtiaz, Muhammad Husnain Ahmad, Ali Gohar
pmc-13239939.description: Recurrent Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is an uncommon variant of immune‐mediated polyradiculoneuropathy. We report a 56‐year‐old male who had two distinct episodes of acute inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy within the span of 3 months. The first episode presented with an episode of ascending paralysis and areflexia, with nerve conduction studies showing marked demyelination. He showed improvement after six sessions of plasma exchange.

pmc-13282436.title: Schwann cell derived extracellular vesicles are multifunctional nanotherapeutic mediators for diabetic oral mucosal wound healing
pmc-13282436.creator: Zihang Xu, Haowen Qi, Xinyu Zhang, Fang Qu, Yaqin Wu, Chun Xu

pmc-13488058.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis reveals molecular regulation of the hypothalamus–pituitary–ovary axis underlying egg production in indigenous chickens
pmc-13488058.creator: Hang Liu, Yinghui Wei, Yanlu Wang, Yuanhao Zhou, Lei Zhang, Weiwu Zhang, Jinghui Fan, Huanhuan Wang

pmc-13581726.title: Psychosocial determinants of exercise behavior in Parkinson’s disease: a mini-review
pmc-13581726.creator: Guanyu Zhang
pmc-13581726.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder, characterized by progressive motor and non-motor symptoms that profoundly impact quality of life. Physical exercise has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological intervention with neuroprotective potential, yet adherence rates remain suboptimal. This mini-review synthesizes current evidence on psychosocial determinants influencing exercise behavior in PD patients.
